summary.text: Daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia. Like her sisters, she was driven mad by Dionysus for doubting Semele's divine affair, and joined Agave in tearing Pentheus apart on Mount Cithaeron.

story.text: When Dionysus came to Thebes, Autonoe and her sisters were the first to be struck with his madness because they had slandered Semele, claiming she had slept with a mortal. They abandoned their homes to rave in Bacchic frenzy on Mount Cithaeron.

When king Pentheus spied on their rites, the frenzied women attacked him. In Ovid's telling, as Pentheus pleaded for his life, Autonoe joined the slaughter alongside her sister Agave, helping to tear his limbs from his body.
